checked_claims: CLAIM 1 ((5,8) is a mandatory open base case because 16 = 2g-2+n) -- CONFIRMED against corpus. SRC-0002 text lines 1222-1234 (proof of Thm 1.5(3)) gives H^BM_k(M_g,n) = 0 for k < 2g and n = 0,1, and for k < 2g-2+n when n >= 2, reducing to the finitely many cases k >= 2g-2+n. For (g,n) = (5,8), 2g-2+n = 16 = k, so the case is exactly at the threshold and does survive the reduction. I re-derived the whole finite list independently and it matches GAP-5: g=3 forces n <= 12 with c(3) = 11 so only M_3,12; g=4 forces n <= 10 <= c(4) = 11 so nothing; g=5 forces n <= 8 with c(5) = 7 so only M_5,8; g=6 forces n <= 6 with c(6) = 5 so only M_6,6; g=7 forces n <= 4 with c(7) = 3 so only M_7,4; g=8 gives n = 0,1,2 (n=0,1 via k >= 2g = 16); g >= 9 is excluded. GAP-5's list is correct and complete.

CLAIM 2 (c(5) = 7, so n = 8 is the first missing pointed case in genus 5) -- CONFIRMED. SRC-0002 text lines 638-641 Table 1 reads g = 0..7 against c(g) = inf,10,10,11,11,7,5,3, so c(5) = 7. Column alignment cross-checks three ways: c(3) = 11 matches line 136, c(7) = 3 matches Theorem 1.10 (line 147), c(6) = 5 matches SRC-0004 Lemma 10.14. SRC-0004 line 2251 Lemma 10.13 states exactly 'If n <= 7, then M5,n has the CKgP and A* = R*'.

CLAIM 3 (Lemma 9.9 gives CKgP for M^3_5,8 and tautological supported classes since 8 <= g+7 = 12) -- CONFIRMED verbatim. SRC-0004 lines 1863-1866: 'Suppose g >= 4 and n <= g + 7. Then M^3_g,n has the CKgP and all classes supported on M^3_g,n are tautological.' The attempt's parenthetical about the hyperelliptic sub-locus is also right: the proof (line 1867) invokes Theorem 6.1 in the range n <= 2g + 6 = 16, and 8 <= 16. Step A is source-verified as stated.

CLAIM 4 (the open tetragonal stratum is the proper surjective image of H^4_4,5,8) -- CONFIRMED. Definition 10.8 (lines 2183-2188) defines H^f_4,g,n = H'_4,g,n minus Supp R^1 pi_* F(f-1), so f = 4 gives F(3) as the attempt writes; Lemma 10.9 (lines 2190-2192) gives H^4_4,5,n = H_4,5,n minus beta^{-1}(M^3_5,n); lines 2244-2249 assert properness of beta'_n with no restriction on n. So Step B transfers to n = 8 legitimately.

CLAIM 5 (the n <= 7 proof needs evaluation surjectivity, guaranteed only for n <= 4f_1 - 2g + 1 = 7) -- CONFIRMED. SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 (lines 2145-2171) and line 2250. But the attempt's framing that 'the numerical criterion fails by exactly one' at n = 8 understates the obstruction: Remark 10.7 (lines 2176-2178) observes f_1 <= (g+3)/2, hence 4f_1 - 2g + 1 <= 7 for EVERY genus. The ceiling of 7 is intrinsic to the method, not a genus-5 off-by-one, so 'extend by one marked point' is the wrong mental model for the repair.

CLAIM 6 (at n = 8, F = (4,4), the Serre-dual degrees are exactly 0) -- ARITHMETIC CONFIRMED, GEOMETRY UNDER-ANALYZED. Line 2169 gives deg = 4f_i + n - 2g - 14, and 16 + 8 - 10 - 14 = 0; the vanishing criterion at line 2167 is the strict inequality 0 > deg, so degree 0 is indeed not covered. However: f_1 + f_2 = g + 3 = 8 with f_1 <= f_2 and f_1 >= 4 forces f_1 = f_2 = 4, so H^4_4,5,n is exactly the single splitting stratum F = (4,4), and consequently W_{f_1} = W_{f_2} = L := O_PE^vee(2) tensor gamma^* O(4). The attempt's 'for at least one i in {1,2}' is therefore one condition, not two, and Step E(1)'s worry about identifying irreducible components largely dissolves: since deg L|_C = 4g + 12 - 4f = 16 and deg omega_C = 8, the degeneracy condition is the single condition Gamma in |L|_C tensor omega_C^vee|, a fixed degree-8 linear series on C with h^0 >= 4. H_D is thus nonempty, of dimension 3 in the fibre C^8 (codimension 5), and is one translate of an Abel-Jacobi locus. This makes GAP-1 substantially softer than 'critical' and simultaneously refutes any hope that H_D is empty.

CLAIM 7 (H_U has CKgP and its image classes push forward tautologically) -- PARTIAL, WITH ONE UNJUSTIFIED STEP. The CKgP half is fine: H^4_4,5,8 intersected with Y|_U is open in Y|_U, the tower (10.10) is unchanged, and Lemma 10.11's proof only ever needs CKgP of B, which is n-independent. Lemma 10.12's excision chain A*((PE^vee)^8) -> A*(U) = A*(Y|_U) -> A*(H_U) also survives. Two defects. (a) Nonemptiness of U, hence of H_U, is assumed silently, yet SRC-0004 lines 2213-2214 explicitly warn that U 'a priori could be empty, and in fact U will be empty when n is too large', and the only supplied tool for U nonempty (Lemma 10.6, applied at line 2215) is precisely the one unavailable at n = 8. The claim is rescuable by the Claim-6 computation above, but the attempt never does it, so its central framing ('the complementary open H_U is under full control') rests on an unproven nonemptiness. (b) 'Its image in M_5,8 minus M^3_5,8 has CKgP' does not follow. beta' restricted to the open H_U is not proper, so SRC-0004 Lemma 3.10 / SRC-0002 Prop 4.2(2) -- both of which require a proper surjective map -- do not apply, and Lemma 10.5's pushforward is only defined for the full proper beta'. This is asserted as a proved Claim (D1) rather than flagged as a gap. It is also self-evidently not available: if it were, combined with beta'(H_U) being all of the tetragonal stratum, the theorem would already be proved.

CLAIM 8 (CKgP for M_5,8 would force W_16 H^16(M_5,8) to be algebraic pure Tate, discharging this RED-0001 input) -- FIRST HALF TRUE, SECOND HALF REFUTED. SRC-0002 Lemma 4.3 (lines 581-591) does give surjectivity of cl onto the direct sum over all k of W_k H^k(X) for X open in a smooth proper DM stack, so CKgP would indeed make W_16 H^16(M_5,8) pure Hodge-Tate, isomorphic to a sum of Q(-8). But degree 16 is not the object the k = 16 base case requires. See strongest_attack. The conditional 'CKgP implies discharge' survives only because Lemma 4.3 delivers all degrees at once; the attempt's explicitly stated weaker fallback target does not survive.

CLAIM 9 (H_D is unclassified, lacks CKgP, and lacks a tautological pushforward) -- CONFIRMED as a real gap in the supplied corpus; nothing in SRC-0004 Section 10 treats the degeneracy locus. Excision A*(H_D) -> A*(H^4_4,5,8) -> A*(H_U) -> 0 confirms that GAP-3 is genuinely needed and not implied by GAP-2. Caveat as in Claim 6: GAP-1 is nearly immediate, so grading GAP-1 and GAP-2 both 'critical' misallocates the remaining difficulty, which sits in GAP-3.

strongest_attack: Cohomology degree versus Borel-Moore homology degree, with a dropped Poincare-duality shift. The attempt selects (g,n) = (5,8) using the HOMOLOGICAL reduction -- SRC-0002 (6.1), H_k(boundary-hat) -> H_k(Mbar_g,n) -> W_{-k} H^BM_k(M_g,n) -> 0, whose open-stack input is the pure part of Borel-Moore homology in degree k, and whose vanishing bound k < 2g-2+n is exactly what makes 16 = 2*5-2+8 a threshold case. It then states the thing to be proved in the wrong degree. With d = dim M_5,8 = 3g-3+n = 20, Poincare duality on the smooth stack gives W_{-16} H^BM_16(M_5,8) isomorphic to (W_24 H^24(M_5,8))(20), since 2d - k = 40 - 16 = 24; and 24 = 4g-4+n is precisely the vcd, which independently confirms the convention because the source's bound k < 2g-2+n is the vcd bound 2d-k > 4g-4+n transported through duality. So the required statement is that the pure part of TOP-degree cohomology H^24(M_5,8) is algebraic, equivalently that codimension-12 cycle classes span it. Step F instead asserts the input is W_16 H^16(M_5,8), a codimension-8 statement, and then makes this explicit and load-bearing: 'Even a proof that only W_16 H^16(M_5,8) is algebraic would suffice for the degree-16 induction at this base case.' That is false, and GAP-4 names the same wrong object, so the attempt's stated fallback goal for future work is mis-specified. The 'and dually' clause in Step F compounds it: W_16 H^16 and W_{-16} H^BM_16 are presented as a Poincare-dual pair, but on a 20-dimensional stack the dual pairs are (H^16, H^BM_24) and (H^24, H^BM_16). The two objects the attempt pairs differ by a degree shift of 2d - 2k = 8 and a twist of Q(4): the correct dual of a sum of Q(-8) in H^16 is a sum of Q(12) in H^BM_24, not the sum of Q(8) written down (that twist is right for weight -16, but belongs to degree 24 on the cohomological side, whose algebraic classes are Q(-12)). A cohomological right-exact sequence with W_k H^k(M) as its input does exist and is used in this very source at line 652, H^{k-2}(boundary-hat) -> H^k(Mbar_3,n) -> W_k H^k(M_3,n) -> 0 -- note the Gysin shift by 2 that the attempt also does not carry -- but its base-case condition is 16 <= 4g-4+n, which selects an INFINITE set of pairs including M_5,n for every n >= 8. So the attempt has imported the selection criterion from the homological reduction and the target object from the cohomological one; under the sequence that actually makes W_16 H^16 the input, 16 = 2g-2+n is not a threshold and the mandatory-ness argument for (5,8) collapses. The two halves of the attempt are inconsistent with each other. This does not overturn the attempt's honest bottom line, which is that nothing is proved and the residual is H_D -- Lemma 4.3 supplies every degree simultaneously, so 'CKgP implies discharge' is unaffected. But it means the correctly-identified target sits at the very top of the vcd range rather than in mid-range, and the attempt never asks the question that identification immediately raises, namely whether known top-degree vanishing for M_g,n makes W_24 H^24(M_5,8) zero and this base case vacuous. The supplied corpus does not settle that (SRC-0002 does not invoke any such vanishing at the threshold, which is weak evidence against vacuity), and I do not assert it; I record it as the check the attempt owed itself and skipped because it was aiming eight degrees low.
